label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, poison-message, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 9 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER idempotent (unchanged), LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS retry -> dead_letter); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: poison-message
case.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer that retries unreadable messages forever (BAD_EVENTS=retry), then one unreadable event from the provider (a payment.updated with its amount as a decimal string): the ledger consumer is stuck on it, and books nothing behind it.
case.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to dead-lettering: the poison goes to the dead-letter topic, the backlog drains, and the money check passes again

alert.name: ConsumerLagHigh
alert.summary: The ledger consumer group is 145 messages behind on the topic provider-events, all partitions together; the threshold is 50. Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, messages up to it were not handled yet: ledger 159.

diagnosis.hypothesis: A malformed provider event sits at provider-events/1@112. Its amount is not positive integer cents. ledger-consumer was redeployed at 10:45:04 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. Under that policy it retries the same message (attempt 9 by 10:46:06, every 15 s) and never commits past it. Every later message on partition 1 queues behind it, so ledger lag rose from 0 at 10:44 to 219 at 10:46. That is why the money check cannot settle. payment-confirmer, with BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, dead-lettered about one event in 10 minutes and keeps processing, which fits the same bad event being set aside there. Still open: what the ledger ran before this deploy (if dead_letter, the deploy turned one bad event into a full partition stall), and which event it is and why its amount is malformed. A provider-side cause is possible; fake-provider was recreated at 10:43:38.

evidence.shows: Ledger consumer lag went from 0 (10:44:10) to 7 (10:45:10) to 219 (10:46:10), confirming the alert.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 10:45:04 with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry, right as lag began. payment-confirmer uses BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter.
ledger-consumer repeatedly fails the same message, provider-events/1@112, with 'amount must be positive integer cents' (attempts 3 to 9), retrying the same message each time.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered about 1 event and otherwise processes normally. The ledger posted events earlier but is now stuck.
klaxon_dead_letters_total returned no series: either the metric has another name or labels, or nothing was dead-lettered there. This does not contradict c6.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings before the 10:45:04 deploy, presumably BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, so it sets aside the poison message at 1@112 and drains the backlog. Then inspect the dead-lettered event, find why its amount is not integer cents (provider-side or receiver-side), book it by hand if it is a real charge or refund, and rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, so lag grows briefly. A dead-lettered event is not booked in the ledger, so the money check may flag it until it is repaired by hand. If the previous settings were not dead_letter, the rollback may not unstick the partition.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=retry). The idempotent handler makes reprocessing safe.
